extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political history and constitutional theory
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing the constitutional defects and proposed reforms of the Florentine republic (and Machiavelli's plan for a 'perfect commonwealth'), including separation of powers, electoral methods, checks and balances, and popular sovereignty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of three powers (separation of powers)
rubrics_metrics.description: His sagacity perceived the necessity of three powers; but he did not see an equal necessity for the separation of the executive power from the legislative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats separation of powers as a fundamental desideratum for constitutional design, while noting debate about how strictly the executive must be separated from the legislature. This frames evaluation of proposed constitutions by whether they allocate distinct powers to separate institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vesting appointment power in an overly large council
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment of officers in the council of a thousand would have ruined all the good effects of the other divisions of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large, unwieldy bodies charged with appointing officers can undermine intended checks and balances; institutional size and appointment procedures should be evaluated for their practical effects on governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of deposing or destroying a tyrant (tyrannicide)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of a nation to depose a tyrant, and to destroy him if he cannot be otherwise deposed, is as clear as any of our ideas of right or wrong... in the Roman republic it was... meritorious and glorious, to kill a tyrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of revolutionary or extreme measures should consider classical and moral justifications: removal of a tyrant can be legitimate when no legal alternative exists, but motivating ends and consequences matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit replacing one tyrant with another
rubrics_metrics.description: It would by no means follow that one tyrant might claim a right to destroy another, merely to take his place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if tyrannicide is justified, any constitution or action that simply substitutes another autocrat is condemned; motives and post-action regime outcomes are critical in judging legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent, regular methods for convening the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of devising any regular method for calling the people together, with a reasonable notification before-hand of the time, place, and subject of deliberation, a little junto of principal citizens concert a plan in secret...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good constitutional practice requires open, regular convening procedures (notice of time/place/subject). Secret, ad-hoc convocations and clandestine juntas are anti-patterns that undermine legitimacy and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad and inclusive franchise (avoid narrow oligarchic electorate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The imborfations are made, and eight hundred names are put in the purses. These alone are citizens; all the rest are to have no vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricted electorates concentrated in a small list of 'citizens' produce oligarchy; a healthy constitution should provide broader, fairer access to political participation or justify limitations transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear voting methods and instructions for representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: These appoint the signori, a small council, for the ordinary administration, and the gonfalonier... no reasonable method of voting for them, no instructions given them; the people huzza, and all is over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural clarity (how officials are chosen, how votes are taken, what instructions/mandates representatives have) is essential. Lack of clear procedures leads to chaotic or capture-prone governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional checks: negative (veto) to executive as constitutional self-defence
rubrics_metrics.description: If you suppose... the gonfalonier possessed of the whole executive power, with a negative upon the legislature, the signori and grand council made separate and independent branches... would not those terrible disorders have been prevented? The negative to the gonfalonier is not proposed... merely as a constitutional instrument of self-defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A veto or negative by the executive (or on the executive) is advocated as a structural check to prevent factional usurpation. Evaluation should consider both preventive value and safeguards against misuse (e.g., removal if abused).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial independence (judges during good behaviour)
rubrics_metrics.description: The judges made during good behaviour, would not those terrible disorders have been prevented? ... the judicial power was always the tool of the prevailing faction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make judges tenure-secure and independent to prevent their use as instruments of prevailing parties; judicial independence is a core criterion for rule of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial responsibility and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: If his ministers are made responsible for the advice they give him, the two houses will always have a remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding ministers accountable for their advice/actions creates institutional remedies for abuses and helps maintain checks between branches; evaluate whether ministerial responsibility mechanisms exist and function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative fiscal control (withholding supplies) as a remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: An honest representative of the commons will always have another remedy, by withholding supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliamentary or representative control over public finances (supply) is an effective check on executive action; presence and enforceability of fiscal controls should be assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent concentration of authority and factional dominance
rubrics_metrics.description: The great council is the centre in which all authority is collected, and he who had most influence in it governed in reality... the council and signori were always divided into parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutions should avoid single centres of de facto authority (even if formally plural) and design institutions to limit factional capture and rotate or balance influence among groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic arms/exercise as a means to preserve liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: To this is to be added, the use and exercise of arms, by which every little nation, if it cannot make extensive conquests, at least may preserve its own liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text presents the civic exercise of arms (militia/exercise) as a historical mechanism small polities used to defend liberty; evaluators should consider the role of citizen defense in regime security and its trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular sovereignty: sovereign power lodged in the citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereign power is lodged, both of right and in fact, in the citizens themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machiavelli's model emphasizes that ultimate sovereignty should reside with the citizenry; constitutional design should be judged by how effectively it realizes popular sovereignty in practice (not just in form).
